title: Expense splitter backend (add expense, compute balances)
declaredInterface: POST /expenses {paidBy, amount, description, splitBetween[]} -> expense; GET /expenses -> list; GET /balances -> {owes: [{from, to, amount}]}; GET /people -> list
assumptions: Node.js + Express REST API, in-memory data store for now (no DB), equal-split among selected people per expense. Frontend to follow later.

completion.whatWasBuilt: Express REST API backend for a group expense splitter: add expenses (payer, amount, equal split among named participants), list/delete expenses, list known people, and a balances endpoint that returns both net per-person balances and a minimized 'who pays who' settlement list. In-memory store, fully unit-tested balance/settlement math, manually verified end-to-end with curl.

decisions.why: Matches the user's initial ask; custom/percentage splits add complexity not yet requested
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Supporting arbitrary per-person amounts from the start

decisions.decision: All money math done in integer cents internally
decisions.why: Avoids floating point drift (e.g. $0.1+$0.2 bugs) when splitting amounts; leftover pennies from uneven splits go to the first N participants
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Doing math directly in float dollars

decisions.decision: GET /balances returns a simplified settlement list (greedy largest-debtor-vs-largest-creditor) in addition to raw net balances
decisions.why: User asked to 'see who owes who' - a minimized settle-up list is more directly useful than a raw pairwise transaction ledger
decisions.alternativesConsidered: Only exposing net balance per person and leaving simplification to the frontend

decisions.decision: No separate people/add-person endpoint; people are derived from expense payer/participant fields
decisions.why: Keeps API surface minimal until a real need (e.g. a people-management UI) appears
decisions.alternativesConsidered: A dedicated People collection with its own CRUD

filesChanged.purpose: Project manifest, express dependency, npm scripts (start/dev/test)
Express app factory wiring routes + JSON middleware, for testability
Entry point, starts the HTTP server on PORT (default 3001)
In-memory expense storage + CRUD + derived people list
Pure net-balance computation and greedy debt-simplification logic
Unit tests for net balance math and debt simplification (node:test)

completion.knownLimitations: No persistence (in-memory, resets on restart), no auth, single implicit currency, equal splits only, no multi-group support.
completion.nextSteps: Build the frontend to consume this API (add-expense form, expense list, balances/settle-up view). Consider adding persistence (SQLite/file-based) if the group's data needs to survive restarts.
